title: The live dispute: is assurance certainty of divine faith, or only of hope/conjecture?
source_text: XLI. Igitur eo redire videtur controversia quae hic inter Protestantes & Romanenses intercedit, An scilicet, certitudo quam fideles Christi gratiae participes habere possunt & debent de sua coram Deo justificatione, sit certitudo Fidei divinae; An vero solum certitudo alterius generis, & alio nomine vocanda. Prius affirmant communi consensu Protestantes: posterius, paucissimis exceptis, Schola Romana, juxta quam ista certitudo non est fidei, sed spei, seu fiduciae, cui competit certitudo certitudine fidei inferior, moralis, scilicet, vel conjecturalis, quae aliquid minus est quam certitudo moralis stricte dicta, quae gravi prorsus argumento & authoritate nititur, cum conjecturalis ex signis probabilibus colligatur; quanquam certitudo illa conjecturalis saepe latiori sensu moralis etiam dicitur.
pass_a_gloss: Therefore the controversy which here intervenes between Protestants and Romanists seems to return to this: whether namely the certainty which faithful partakers of Christ’s grace can and ought to have concerning their justification before God is the certainty of divine Faith; or whether only a certainty of another kind, and to be called by another name. The former Protestants affirm by common consent: the latter, with very few exceptions, the Roman School, according to which that certainty is not of faith but of hope, or trust, to which belongs a certainty inferior to the certainty of faith—moral, namely, or conjectural, which is something less than moral certainty strictly so called, which rests on altogether weighty argument and authority, whereas the conjectural is gathered from probable signs; although that conjectural certainty is often in a wider sense also called moral.
pass_b_english: The real clash is nomenclature and grade: divine-faith certainty versus hope’s moral or conjectural certainty.
Rome (almost unanimously) ranks status-assurance below article-faith; Protestants commonly call it faith’s certainty.
